01 — PROFILE

Automates the drudgery.
Serves the person.

A combination that fits public-service IT and client support: technical enough to rebuild the process with AI, experienced enough to know what the person using it actually needs.

About

Aidan Cafazzo is an Information Technology graduate whose instinct is to automate the manual process in front of him. Starting from a manual timetable, he built Schedule Sensei — a prototype web-based scheduling and time-tracking system — using AI-assisted development (Lovable and Claude Code) with a Supabase backend, complete with rules-based security and audit trails.

That builder's instinct sits on a service foundation. At the LCBO from 2020 to 2024 he served the public at volume — 100+ transactions per shift, handling $5K–$10K+ — and with Elections Canada he served as a Deputy Returning Officer in 2019 and 2025, a role built on accuracy, procedure, and public trust. He now works as a Receiving Champion at Healthy Planet (June 2026 to present).

His Minor in Cognitive Science shapes both sides: how people think, where processes break down, and how a well-designed system prevents the error instead of blaming the user.

CRA Taxpayer Inquiry Case Tracker

A concept prototype in Government of Canada / Canada Revenue Agency styling that mirrors the daily work of taxpayer services: logging inquiries, triaging them, and tracking each case against a service standard. It reads 12 fictional cases live from a Google Sheet — synthetic demo data only, refreshed on every open.

  • Live sheet-backed queue — search and filter cases by status, category, and channel, with status counts and a full case-detail view.
  • SLA watchlist — cases flagged at risk or past their due date surface first, the way a real queue is worked.
  • Escalation built in — cases needing senior review are marked Escalated, with the reason documented in the case notes.
  • Honest demo limits — adding a case is local to the browser session only and labelled as such; nothing is written back to the sheet.

CRA Benefits Eligibility Checker

A concept prototype in Government of Canada / CRA styling: a guided questionnaire that compares a few plain answers against CRA benefit rules held in a Google Sheet, and returns “may qualify” results with the exact published amounts and official canada.ca links. Synthetic demo data only.

  • Five-step questionnaire — residency and filing, children in your care, household and income range, work, and disability — all in plain language.
  • Rules read live from the sheet — Canada Child Benefit, Child Disability Benefit, Groceries and Essentials Benefit, Canada Workers Benefit, and the Disability Tax Credit, with amounts copied exactly as published.
  • Source-linked results — every result links to the official canada.ca page. Guidance only, never presented as an entitlement.
  • The honest edges — the ended Canada Carbon Rebate is shown only as closed, and programs CRA doesn't administer are never labelled as CRA benefits. Answers stay in the browser tab; no SIN or exact income is ever asked.

AI BUILD — PROTOTYPE Claude Code Supabase Lovable

Schedule Sensei

Schedule Sensei grew out of a manual timetable: a prototype shift-work scheduling and time-tracking system built with AI-assisted development — Lovable and Claude Code on a Supabase backend — designed to give employees and managers one system instead of paper and spreadsheets.

  • Scheduling, in one place — employee availability and seniority tracked in the system, with schedule generation and payroll export built in.
  • For employees — download your individual schedule, and switch shifts where management has enabled it.
  • Logged changes — shift switches and edits are recorded with an audit trail, not lost in a group chat.
  • For managers — create timetables and manage the roster from one interface.
  • Payroll-ready — download total hours worked per employee for upload into the pay system.
DEMO STATUS Prototype — no live demo at this time. The hosted demo is offline: its backend is unreachable and sign-in fails, so Schedule Sensei is listed as a prototype, with the screenshot at right from the working build. The working demos on this page are the two CRA concept prototypes above.
